purpose: Add eight source-exact Ira D. Sankey hymn-history excerpts for family worship, children's ministry, sacred song, calling, evangelism, and compassionate visitation.

defaults.author: Ira D. Sankey
defaults.sourceTitle: My Life and the Story of the Gospel Hymns and of Sacred Songs and Solos
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1907 Sunday School Times Company edition is public domain in the United States; every excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.

entries.title: The First Hymn He Remembered
entries.text: The first hymn I remember having heard was from the lips of my beloved mother
entries.slideText: The first hymn I remember having heard was from the lips of my beloved mother
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 13
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed biographical illustration of the lasting influence of sacred song in the home.
entries.reviewNote: Do not make one family pattern a universal command. Teach parental discipleship from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Hymns Around the Family Fire
entries.text: As a boy, it was one of my chief joys to meet with other members of our family around the great log fire in the old homestead
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 13
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed scene-setter for family worship, Christian memory, or teaching children through song.
entries.reviewNote: The scene is autobiography, not Scripture. Ground family instruction and singing in the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: A Hymn at Work in the Soul
entries.text: I have known a hymn to do God's work in a soul when every other instrumentality has failed.
entries.slideText: I have known a hymn to do God's work in a soul
entries.author: George F. Pentecost, quoted by Ira D. Sankey
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historical testimony to the pastoral influence of biblically faithful hymns.
entries.reviewNote: Songs are not independent saving instruments. Evaluate every lyric by KJV Scripture and keep salvation centered on Christ and the gospel.

entries.title: A Sunday-School Teacher's Early Influence
entries.text: my first impressions were received from that man when I was very young.
entries.slideText: my first impressions were received from that man
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 14
entries.recommendedUse: Use with the surrounding story of Mr. Frazer leading children to Sunday school as an attributed illustration of quiet influence.
entries.reviewNote: The excerpt depends on its stated narrative context. Do not present childhood impressions as conversion; Sankey distinguishes his later conversion.

entries.title: Preparation for Lifework
entries.text: I was making preparation for the work in which I was to spend my life.
entries.slideText: preparation for the work in which I was to spend my life
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 15
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed reflection on how ordinary service and cultivated skill can prepare a believer for later ministry.
entries.reviewNote: Avoid reading providence infallibly from hindsight. Teach faithful preparation and service from KJV Scripture.

entries.title: When the Congregation Joined Heartily
entries.text: The congregation joined heartily and a brighter aspect seemed to be given to the meeting.
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 21
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historical illustration of the difference between performed music and congregational participation.
entries.reviewNote: A brighter atmosphere is not proof of spiritual fruit. Measure worship by truth, reverence, and KJV Scripture.

entries.title: Reaching the Masses
entries.text: Here was a man who could successfully reach the masses while others were talking about it.
entries.slideText: reach the masses while others were talking about it
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 23
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed observation about Moody's practical evangelistic action after explaining the historical setting.
entries.reviewNote: Do not equate visible crowds with spiritual success. Define faithful gospel work from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Bible and Hymn at the Sickbed
entries.text: I am going to read a few words from the Bible, but first I want my friend, Sankey, to sing a little hymn for you.
entries.slideText: read a few words from the Bible
entries.author: D. L. Moody, quoted by Ira D. Sankey
entries.sourceLocator: Sankey's Story of His Own Life, page 24
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historical illustration of simple, personal ministry to a sick family through Scripture and song.
entries.reviewNote: The order of Bible reading and singing is descriptive, not prescriptive. Keep Scripture primary and practice pastoral sensitivity.
